/-!
# Erdős Problem 266

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/266](https://www.erdosproblems.com/266)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos266

open Filter

/--
Let $a_n$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges.
There exists some integer $t \ge 1$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ is irrational.

This was disproven by Kovač and Tao in [KoTa24].

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos266.lean#L306"]
theorem erdos_266 :
    ¬ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ((∀ n : ℕ, a n ≥ 1) ∧ Summable ((1 : ℝ) / a ·) →
      ∃ t ≥ (1 : ℕ), Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t)) := by
  sorry

/--
In fact, Kovač and Tao proved in [KoTa24] that there exists a strictly increasing
sequence $a_n$ of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ converges to a rational
number for all $t \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $t \ne -a_n$ for any $n$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_266.variants.all_rationals:
    ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ a 0 ≥ 1 ∧
      (∀ t : ℚ, (¬ ∃ n : ℕ, t = -(a n)) →
        (∃ q : ℚ, HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))) q)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos266

reformulations.difference: States the recorded negative resolution as a negated universal irrationality assertion, rather than explicitly exhibiting a sequence whose positive integral shifted series converge to rational numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Negating the universal assertion produces a positive reciprocal-summable sequence with no irrational positive integral shifted sum. For every such shift, 0 ≤ 1/(a_n+t) ≤ 1/a_n, so the shifted series is genuinely summable: the default value of tsum cannot intervene. Not being irrational is equivalent to equalling a rational number. The exact equivalence with an explicit rational-HasSum counterexample was proved in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Uses unconditional HasSum for ordinary series convergence and expresses positivity by a 0 ≥ 1 together with StrictMono a.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Strict monotonicity makes a 0 ≥ 1 equivalent to positivity at every index. It also implies a n ≥ n, so for each fixed rational shift the summands are nonnegative beyond a finite prefix. Consequently ordinary convergence and unconditional HasSum coincide. A full equivalence with the positive-sequence, ordered-partial-sum formulation was proved in scratch.lean. The pole condition was also proved equivalent to every real denominator being nonzero.
